author.match: Match each poem to its poet.
author.odd: Three of these were written by {value}. Which one wasn't?

rows.label: Ramayana
rows.author: Valmiki
rows.description: An ancient Hindu epic composed by Valmiki which narrates the life story of Lord Rama.
rows.hook: follows an exiled prince who wages a great war to rescue his kidnapped wife from a demon king

rows.label: Paradise Lost
rows.author: John Milton
rows.hook: tells of a rebellious angel's fall and the expulsion of the first man and woman from their garden home

rows.label: Mahabharata
rows.author: Vyasa
rows.hook: recounts a great war between two branches of a royal family, fought on a sacred battlefield

rows.label: Ozymandias
rows.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
rows.hook: describes a crumbling desert statue whose boastful inscription mocks the ruin of its own forgotten king

rows.label: Bhagavad Gita
rows.author: Vyasa
rows.hook: records a battlefield dialogue between a warrior prince and his divine charioteer about duty and destiny

rows.label: Aeneid
rows.author: Virgil
rows.hook: follows a Trojan hero's journey to found the city that would become Rome

rows.label: The Canterbury Tales
rows.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
rows.description: collection of stories written in Middle English by Geoffrey Chaucer
rows.hook: gathers a band of pilgrims trading stories on their journey to a holy shrine

rows.label: Jabberwocky
rows.author: Lewis Carroll
rows.hook: invents nonsense words to tell of a monster slain by a hero with a vorpal sword

rows.label: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
rows.author: Pearl poet
rows.hook: follows a warrior who accepts a beheading challenge from a mysterious emerald-skinned stranger

rows.label: The Raven
rows.author: Edgar Allan Poe
rows.description: narrative poem by Edgar Allan Poe
rows.hook: features a talking bird repeating a single haunting word to a man grieving his lost love

rows.label: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
rows.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
rows.hook: tells of a sailor cursed after killing an albatross, forced to recount his tale to a wedding guest

rows.label: Metamorphoses
rows.author: Ovid
rows.hook: collects myths in which people are transformed into animals, plants, and stars

rows.label: And did those feet in ancient time
rows.author: William Blake
rows.hook: asks whether Christ once walked upon English soil, and gave rise to a stirring national hymn

rows.label: The Tyger
rows.author: William Blake
rows.hook: questions what immortal power could have forged a fearsome predator's perfect symmetry

rows.label: O Captain! My Captain!
rows.author: Walt Whitman
rows.description: poem by Walt Whitman on the death of Abraham Lincoln
rows.hook: mourns a fallen leader who guided the ship of state safely to port, only to die as it arrives

rows.label: The Road Not Taken
rows.author: Robert Frost
rows.hook: reflects on choosing between two diverging paths in an autumn wood

rows.label: The Charge of the Light Brigade
rows.author: Alfred Tennyson
rows.hook: honors a doomed cavalry assault into enemy cannon fire after a battlefield order was misunderstood

rows.label: Piers Plowman
rows.author: William Langland
rows.description: Middle English allegorical narrative poem by William Langland
rows.hook: uses a series of dream visions to guide a search for religious truth in medieval England

rows.label: Kubla Khan
rows.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
rows.hook: describes a fantastical pleasure dome imagined in a dream and left unfinished after an interruption

rows.label: Layla and Majnun
rows.author: Nizami Ganjavi
rows.description: story of Arab origin, about the 7th-century Arabic poet Qays ibn al-Mulawwah and his lover Layla bint Mahdi
rows.hook: tells of a poet driven to madness by his forbidden love for a woman he could never marry

rows.label: Telegony
rows.author: Eugammon of Cyrene
rows.description: poem written by Eugammon of Cyrene
rows.hook: tells how a hero is fatally wounded by his own unknown son, neither realizing who the other is

rows.label: The Lady of Shalott
rows.author: Alfred Tennyson
rows.hook: follows a cursed weaver in a tower who dies floating downriver after glimpsing a knight

rows.label: Meghadūta
rows.author: Kalidasa
rows.hook: has an exiled spirit ask a passing raincloud to carry a message of love to his distant wife

rows.label: In Flanders Fields
rows.author: John McCrae
rows.hook: has fallen soldiers speak from their graves among blooming poppies, urging the living to keep fighting

rows.label: The Song of Roland
rows.author: Turold
rows.hook: recounts a knight's last stand in a mountain ambush, blowing his horn for help only when it is too late
